title: Uniqueness of the global orientation
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ and $\kappa(t)$ be as in
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. The restriction of the
homomorphism group to
geometric points is an
injective map

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,\Lambda)}
\bigl(\Lambda_Y,Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\bigr)
\longrightarrow
\prod_{\bar y\to Y}H^2_{s(\bar y)}(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},\Lambda(1)),
$$

whose image contains the family with every component $1\in\Lambda$ (by
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] and the normalization of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]). Consequently
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ is the unique global morphism whose pullback to
every geometric point is the normalized class $1$.

proof.text:
Use the current [def-pur-conventions]: $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ is the finite coefficient ring, $A_Y$ is its degree-zero constant coefficient unit, and $Rs^!$ denotes the constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] on the stated bounded constructible categories. The input $A_X(1)$ and the support object below are the finite-level objects of those conventions. Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}$, $p:X\to Y$, $\pi=pj$, and $F=Rs^!A_X(1)[2]$. Use precisely [def-pur-affine-line-datum], including its present coefficient-level convention $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$ and the specified etale/pro-etale identification of the twist and Kummer class; no integral or rational coefficients are asserted here. The base is separated finite type over $k$, as assumed in the item. By [lem-pur-gysin-structure], $F\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $\mathcal H^i(F)=0$ for $i\ne0$. Put $L=\mathcal H^0(F)$. Applying [lem-pur-concentrated-complex-shift](1) with $r=0$ gives $F\simeq L[0]$. The fully faithful degree-zero embedding of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] therefore identifies
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,A)}(A_Y,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_Y}(A_Y,L)=\Gamma(Y,L).$$
The last bijection sends a sheaf map to the image of $1$; its inverse sends a section $v$ to $a\mapsto av$, on every object of the site. This also explains why the Hom group is a module of global sections, not a rank-one sheaf or necessarily a rank-one module.

proof.text:
By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](4), $A_X(1)$ lies in $D^b_c(X,A)$; so [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) gives $B\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)\subset D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $\nu_X^*B\cong A_X(1)$. Apply [lem-pur-retracted-support-localization-comparison] to this $B$ and $K=A_X(1)$; then $j^*K=A_U(1)$ is the pro-etale twist carrying the class $\kappa(t)$ of [def-pur-affine-line-datum]. Its hypotheses hold: $p$ is affine of finite type, $s$ is the closed section $t=0$, and $j$ is the principal open $D(t)$; all schemes are separated finite type over $k$. We obtain the triangle
$$Rs^!A_X(1)\longrightarrow Rp_*A_X(1)\longrightarrow R\pi_*A_U(1)\longrightarrow Rs^!A_X(1)[1].$$
The cohomology sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and the vanishing $R^1p_*A_X(1)=R^2p_*A_X(1)=0$ in [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](1) give an isomorphism
$$\delta:R^1\pi_*A_U(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^2(Rs^!A_X(1))=L.$$
Clause (2) of [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer] gives the isomorphism $A_Y\to R^1\pi_*A_U(1)$ carrying $1$ to the edge image of $\kappa(t)$. Compose it with $\delta$ to obtain an isomorphism $o:A_Y\to L$. The boundary-edge equality of the comparison lemma sends this section to the edge image of $\partial\kappa(t)$. By [lem-pur-gysin-structure] and the definition of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation], that is precisely the section corresponding to $\mathcal H^0(\operatorname{pur}_s)$. Maps out of $A_Y$ are determined by the image of $1$, so $o=\mathcal H^0(\operatorname{pur}_s)$. Thus the actual Kummer orientation trivializes $L$.

proof.text:
Combining the degree-zero Hom identification of step 1 with $o^{-1}$ of step 2 identifies every $\varphi:A_Y\to F$ with a unique section $a\in\Gamma(Y,A_Y)$. Explicitly the endomorphism $m_a:A_Y\to A_Y$, $b\mapsto ab$, satisfies
$$\varphi=\operatorname{pur}_s\circ m_a.$$
Indeed both sides correspond to the sheaf map $o\circ m_a$ under the fully faithful single-complex embedding. The orientation corresponds to the section $1$. This is a calculation of sheaf maps on the degree-zero representatives, so it does not require a claim that geometric pullback is faithful on an arbitrary derived category.

source.place: Steps 1–4; expanded with the unit rank-one calculation

proof.text:
Fix $g:\bar y=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and let $h:X'=\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}\to X$, $p':X'\to\bar y$ and $s':\bar y\hookrightarrow X'$ be the base changes, so $h^{-1}(s(Y))=s'(\bar y)$. Put $K=A_X(1)$. By [lem-pur-supported-hom] and the counit $\epsilon:s_*Rs^!K\to K$ of the finite-level adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (its source $A_Y$ is bounded below of etale origin), $\varphi$ corresponds to the supported class $c(\varphi)\in H^2_{s(Y)}(X,K)$ represented by $\epsilon[2]\circ s_*\varphi:s_*A_Y\to K[2]$; the component $r_{\bar y}(\varphi)$ is its pullback $h^*c(\varphi)\in H^2_{s'(\bar y)}(X',A_{X'}(1))$ along the map of pairs, which is natural in the coefficient complex [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. Put $b=p^{-1}a\in\Gamma(X,A_X)$. Multiplication by a global section of the commutative coefficient ring sheaf commutes with every chain map of complexes of $A_X$-modules, hence with every morphism of $D(X,A)$, each being a roof of such maps. Since $s^{-1}b=(ps)^{-1}a=a$, $s_*m_a$ is multiplication by $b$ on $s_*A_Y$. With step 3,
$$\epsilon[2]\circ s_*\varphi=\epsilon[2]\circ s_*\operatorname{pur}_s\circ b=b_{K[2]}\circ\epsilon[2]\circ s_*\operatorname{pur}_s,$$
so naturality of [lem-pur-supported-hom] in its coefficient gives $c(\varphi)=H^2_{s(Y)}(b_K)\,c(\operatorname{pur}_s)$, and naturality of the pullback gives $r_{\bar y}(\varphi)=H^2_{s'(\bar y)}(h^*b_K)\,r_{\bar y}(\operatorname{pur}_s)$. Here $h^*b_K$ is multiplication by $h^{-1}b=p'^{-1}g^{-1}a$. Let $m_a^{\mathrm{et}}$ be the etale endomorphism of $A_{Y_{\mathrm{et}}}$ with $\nu_Y^*m_a^{\mathrm{et}}=m_a$; it exists by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1),(2), [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $g^*m_a=\nu^*g^{-1}m_a^{\mathrm{et}}$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] this is multiplication by the element $a_{\bar y}\in A$ given by the stalk of $m_a^{\mathrm{et}}$ at $\bar y$ applied to $1$. Thus $h^{-1}b$ is the constant $a_{\bar y}$, and the $A$-linear functor $H^2_{s'(\bar y)}$ sends multiplication by it to multiplication by $a_{\bar y}$:
$$r_{\bar y}(\varphi)=a_{\bar y}\,r_{\bar y}(\operatorname{pur}_s).$$
The normalization in [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and the $A$-linear residue isomorphism $\rho_{\bar y}$ of [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] yield
$$\rho_{\bar y}(r_{\bar y}(\varphi))=a_{\bar y}.$$
No base-change isomorphism for the exceptional functor, no finite exchange comparison, and no finite-type hypothesis on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is used.

proof.text: Suppose $r_{\bar y}(\varphi)=r_{\bar y}(\psi)$ for every geometric point, and write $a,b\in\Gamma(Y,A_Y)$ for their sections in step 3. Step 4 gives $a_{\bar y}=b_{\bar y}$ everywhere. We justify the section test in the correct category. The constant sheaf $A_Y$ is the exact comparison pullback of its etale model, by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1),(2). Full faithfulness on $D^+$ in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], together with [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], identifies its pro-etale sheaf endomorphisms with its etale sheaf endomorphisms. These identifications respect geometric inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Let $f$ be the etale endomorphism corresponding to $m_a-m_b$. Its stalk maps are zero by step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]. On underlying abelian sheaves put $I=\operatorname{im}f$. Exactness of etale geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives $I_{\bar y}=\operatorname{im}f_{\bar y}=0$. Applying [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to I$ gives $I=0$, hence $f=0$, hence $m_a=m_b$ and $a=b$. Step 3 then gives $\varphi=\psi$. This proves injectivity of the displayed restriction homomorphism. The test was made on etale sheaves and transported by full faithfulness; geometric stalks need not be conservative on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Steps 1–4; expanded with the unit rank-one calculation

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{pur}_s$ exists by [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and has every geometric component equal to the class corresponding to $1\in A$ under [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]. Therefore the all-ones family lies in the image. If another morphism has these same components, injectivity from step 5 makes it equal to $\operatorname{pur}_s$. No connectedness of $Y$ was assumed: on a disconnected base sections can take different values on different components and the product tests each of them. If $Y$ is empty, its sheaf module category and the Hom group are zero and the empty product is the zero group, so the same assertion and uniqueness hold.
